blogs.title: Acquired Ondine’s Curse: When a Chiari Malformation Takes Your Sleep Breath Away
blogs.description: This post demystifies how cerebellar tonsillar descent in Chiari I can compress brainstem respiratory centers, producing an acquired central hypoventilation syndrome that mimics Ondine’s curse. It contrasts this with congenital CCHS, outlines clinical clues such as preserved voluntary breathing and silent desaturation, and explains how to differentiate from other central apnea etiologies.

blogs.title: Neurogenic Dysphagia in Chiari Malformation: Unmasking the Silent Choking Syndrome
blogs.description: Explores the neurogenic dysphagia often missed in Chiari I, detailing the mechanisms behind equal solid–liquid impairment, the pitfalls of routine endoscopy, and the diagnostic power of videofluoroscopic swallow studies. Emphasizes early neurology referral to prevent prolonged diagnostic delay.

blogs.title: The Old CT’s New Diagnosis: How Re‑Reviewing Past Imaging Solved a Decade‑Long Mystery
blogs.description: Shows how a 14‑year‑old CT scan, initially read as normal, actually contained subtle evidence of a crowded foramen magnum. Highlights common radiologic miss‑s, the value of re‑examining archived studies in unexplained neurology, and guidelines for imaging signs that should trigger a Chiari work‑up.

blogs.title: Vertex Allodynia and Burning Vertex: Scalp Pain as a Red Flag for Chiari Malformation
blogs.description: Discusses the uncommon presentation of vertex allodynia and the so‑called “burning vertex” syndrome in Chiari patients. Reviews symptom patterns, pathophysiological links to occipital nerve irritation or small‑fiber involvement, and outlines diagnostic nerve blocks and conservative pain treatments.

blogs.title: Sleep‑Apnoea in Chiari: Why Type‑III Polysomnography Can Mislead Clinicians
blogs.description: A technical dive into why non‑EEG polysomnography often under‑estimates central hypoventilation in Chiari I, using the case’s type‑III study to illustrate potential false minima. Presents evidence for full laboratory PSG with capnography and video, and discusses the implications for management.

blogs.title: Posterior Fossa Decompression vs Watchful Waiting: Surgical Timing in Symptomatic Chiari Malformation
blogs.description: Examines decision‑making for decompression surgery versus conservative management, drawing on the patient’s trajectory to illustrate selection criteria, risk–benefit analysis, and monitoring strategies. Summarizes current guidelines and surgical outcome data for patients who decline or defer surgery.
